objective: Improve titles and thumbnails without promising an experience the audio does not deliver.

metric_rules.ctr: Measures packaging response from impressions; it is not a music-quality score.
metric_rules.average_view_duration: Measures minutes listened per view; it is the primary continuity signal for long-form mixes.
metric_rules.average_percentage_viewed: Provides context for duration, but must not replace absolute minutes listened.
metric_rules.impressions: Measures reach; low impressions with strong retention is a distribution problem, not proof that the mix failed.
metric_rules.decision_rule: Diagnose CTR, reach and listening continuity separately before changing title, thumbnail or audio.

title: Lead with the real listener use case: Relaxing, Study, Late-Night or Coffeehouse.
State the actual duration and musical style; never promise upbeat energy for soft music.
Do not use clickbait, fake claims, excessive keywords or unsupported genre labels.
thumbnail: Use one clear adult cinematic focal subject or scene.
Keep text optional, short and readable at mobile size; do not bake text into generated artwork.
Preserve the approved character and visual language; no anime-derived rendering.

audio_feedback_rules: Low average view duration with early exits is a continuity/mix investigation first.
Abrupt rhythm, key, energy or instrumentation changes trigger rejection before packaging tests.
A high CTR cannot rescue a mix that loses listeners in the opening minutes.
pdca: Plan a single packaging or audio hypothesis.
Check CTR, impressions, average view duration and early-retention curve together.
Act by retaining, revising or rejecting the hypothesis and recording the evidence.
